content: # 2.1 Design Variables & Chromosome Structure. This figure defines the mapping mechanism from the physical 3D frame to the genetic representation. Members are categorized into hierarchical groups: columns by planar position (Corner, Edge, Interior) and beams by functional role (Exterior, Interior). these physical groups are then encoded into a unified chromosome vector following the exact sequence of column section indices, binary rotation flags, and beam section indices, ensuring a structured search space for optimization.
visual_intent: Figure 1: Schematic of the encoding process. (a) 3D isometric and plan views of the RC frame showing the classification of members into Column groups (Corner, Edge, Interior) and Beam groups (Exterior, Interior). (b) The transformation into a Genetic Chromosome, illustrating the sequential serialization order: [Column Section IDs] -> [Column Rotation Flags] -> [Beam Section IDs]. Explicit mapping arrows show how each physical group is linked to its designated segment in the chromosome.

content: # 3.1 Optimization Methodology. The proposed framework integrates three major components as shown in the flowchart: (1) Stage 1: Database Construction, where a section library is generated and pre-calculated; (2) User Input, defining structural geometry, loads, and GA parameters; and (3) Stage 2: Optimization, which executes an iterative fitness evaluation loop including 3D FEA modeling, structural analysis, and constraint-dominance based NSGA-II operations. The framework specifically handles constraint violations through a penalty application mechanism before yielding the final Pareto-optimal front.
visual_intent: Figure 2: Comprehensive flowchart of the optimization framework divided into two main stages and a user input block. Stage 1 (Database Construction) shows steps 1-4 (Define constraints -> Store in DB). User Input includes GA params, shape, and loads. Stage 2 (Optimization) detail steps 5-9: Initial population -> Fitness evaluation (6.1 Build model, 6.2 Analysis, 6.3 Check constraints, 6.4 Calculate objectives) -> Decision on violation (Yes: Apply penalty, No: Continue) -> Step 7 NSGA-II operations -> Step 8 Next gen selection -> Step 9 Termination check (Loop or Final Pareto Front).

content: # 4.1 Integrated Framework for Practical Section Database Generation and Multi-Criteria Filtering. This figure illustrates the three-stage automated pipeline for constructing a project-specific discrete search space. (Stage 1) Automated Detailing Engine: Implements ACI 318-19 seismic provisions, including the 1.2*Mcr cracking moment constraint for beams and the FB/LR (Front-Back/Left-Right) pairing strategy for column rebar symmetry. (Stage 2) High-Fidelity Performance Quantification: Executes non-linear section analysis based on strain compatibility to derive P-M interaction surfaces and nominal flexural strengths. It simultaneously computes environmental and economic metrics (Cost, CO2) and extracts the 'PM Volume' as a unified performance indicator. (Stage 3) Smart Search Space Reduction: Employs a Pareto-based non-dominated sorting algorithm to filter out structurally inefficient sections within each reinforcement ratio bin, resulting in a condensed, high-performance database ready for global optimization.
visual_intent: Figure 4: Detailed Flowchart of the Section Database Pipeline. [Stage 1: Variable Sampling] -> Sampling of (b, h, fck, fy, rebar sizes). -> [Stage 2: Detailing Engine]. Two logic paths: (1) 'Beam: N-layer rebar distribution & 1.2*Mcr cracking check' and (2) 'Column: Corner + Side (FB/LR) pair generation & Clear spacing check'. -> [Stage 3: High-Fidelity Analysis]. 'Beams: Mn calculation' and 'Columns: P-M curves (Mz, My) via Strain Compatibility'. Sub-outputs: 'Unit Weight (for FEA)', 'Cost/CO2 (Materials)', and 'PM Volume (Performance Metric)'. -> [Stage 4: Smart Reduction Gate]. Logic: 'Binning by Reinforcement Ratio' -> 'Non-dominated Sorting (Maximize PM Volume vs. Minimize Cost/CO2)'. -> [End: Project-Specific Discrete Database]. Use specific icons for filters and analysis kernels, with color coding for Beam vs. Column processes.

content: # 4.2 Implementation of Practical Load Scenarios using Checkerboard Patterns. This figure displays the representative plan-view load patterns applied to the 4, 6, and 8-story benchmark structures. The checkerboard configuration is strategically employed to simulate the structural imbalance and eccentricity caused by variations in floor usage (e.g., lobby, office, residential) and non-uniform live load distribution. By alternating loaded and unloaded spans across different floors and zones, the framework tests the robustness of the optimized member orientations and section capacities under realistic worst-case gravity load scenarios, providing the physical rationale for the inclusion of column rotation variables.
visual_intent: Figure 6: Representative plan-view layouts of checkerboard load patterns for (a) 4-story, (b) 6-story, and (c) 8-story benchmark structures. The diagrams show a 2D grid plan for each case, where specific floor bays are shaded or hatched to represent areas under maximum live load, while adjacent bays remain unshaded. Labels indicate the differentiated live load intensities applied to each floor group (e.g., 5.0 kN/m2 for lower floors vs. 2.0 kN/m2 for upper floors). Contrasting colors or hatching styles are used to distinguish between loaded zones, emphasizing the spatial imbalance that triggers biaxial bending and necessitates optimal column orientation.
